reasons.A: Closest sentence movement: very short declaratives and fragments in quick runs, plain no-contraction diction, and a flat, understated close like the passage's; only slightly heavier on fragments than the original.
reasons.B: Right plain register and dry asides ('Probably the second.', 'I will not say which.') match the stance, but sentences run a little longer and the diary-moral ending is neater than the author's.
reasons.C: Long, smoothly joined literary sentences, similes and explicit sentiment ('oddly touching', 'more moving') are far from the author's clipped, deadpan rhythm.
